judgments.reason: Solar provides 16.2% out of the 16.9% total renewable generation, accounting for roughly 96% of all renewables.
The verified data shows natural gas comprises 79.7% of total generation, directly supporting the conclusion of heavy single-fuel dependence.

requirements.evidence: Israel generated 16.9% of its electricity from renewables in 2025, up from 1.9% in 2015, an increase of 15 percentage points.
requirements.reason: The report provides the 2025 renewables share, the 2015 share, and the exact percentage-point change.

requirements.evidence: Coal fell from 45.4% of generation in 2015 to just 3.4% in 2025
requirements.reason: The report specifies both historical and current shares of coal in Israel's electricity mix.

requirements.evidence: Among Mediterranean peers, Greece reached 49.7% renewables in 2025 and Cyprus 27.8%.
requirements.reason: The report compares Israel's renewable figures against two Mediterranean peers (Greece and Cyprus) for 2025.

requirements.evidence: Total generation grew from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh, about 28%.
requirements.reason: The report details total generation in TWh for both 2015 and 2025 as well as the percentage growth.

requirements.evidence: Key risk: with roughly 80% of electricity coming from gas, Israel depends heavily on a single fuel.
requirements.reason: The report highlights natural gas single-fuel reliance as a key risk directly grounded in the 79.7% generation figure.
